About {{THERAPIST_NAME}} — an intentional, focused practice

I work with adults navigating anxiety, transitions, relationship shifts, and burnout. My style is pragmatic, compassionate, and oriented toward skills you can use between sessions.

{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}} Or call {{PHONE}}

Core commitments

These guide the work I offer. They reflect how I show up in session and how I structure change outside of it.

  • Clarity: We set focused goals together and track progress.
  • Safety: Emotional safety and confidentiality are central.
  • Practicality: You’ll leave sessions with concrete strategies you can apply.

What clients say

"Calm, precise, and deeply present. I learned tools that helped me get unstuck." — A. R.

"A pragmatic approach that honored my experience while offering clear steps forward." — M. K.

How I work in sessions

I combine evidence-informed techniques with an individualized coaching lens. Typical methods include:

  • CBT-informed skill building for anxiety and worry.
  • Trauma-sensitive stabilization and somatic awareness.
  • Attachment-informed relational work for partnerships and family dynamics.

Modalities: {{MODALITIES}}

Common practical questions

I hear practical concerns often. Here are brief answers.

  • Insurance: I am a private-pay clinician; receipts can be provided for out-of-network reimbursement.
  • Time: Sessions are typically 45–55 minutes. We’ll collaborate on pacing.
  • Effectiveness: Therapy is a process; I focus on measurable, short-term goals and regular review.

Welcome packet

Request a complimentary welcome packet that explains what to expect, how I protect confidentiality, and a short worksheet to begin clarifying goals.

Get the packet

Ready to start?

If this feels like a good fit, schedule an initial consultation. I offer focused intake sessions designed to clarify needs and create a 6–8 session plan.

{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}

Confidentiality & privacy: Conversations are confidential except where disclosure is required by law (e.g., imminent risk of harm). For full details, ask for the practice privacy summary.

Crisis disclaimer: If you are in crisis or at risk of harm, call local emergency services or go to your nearest emergency room. Email is not monitored for emergencies.

Scope & boundaries: I provide outpatient psychotherapy for adults. I do not provide emergency services, complex forensic evaluations, or court testimony.

Contact: {{EMAIL}} • {{PHONE}}

Areas of focus

Specialized, evidence-informed care for adults looking to reduce distress and build sustained coping capacity.

Common concerns I help with

  • Anxiety & worry: Panic, generalized worry, anticipatory stress.
  • Trauma reactions: Post-traumatic stress symptoms, intrusive memories, hypervigilance (trauma-informed, stabilization first).
  • Relationship strain: Communication patterns, attachment-related hurt, conflict navigation.
  • Life transitions: Career changes, relocation, parenting shifts.
  • Burnout & overwhelm: Work-related stress and chronic exhaustion.

Modalities & format

I blend approaches to match each person's needs and pace. Typical modalities include:

  • Cognitive-behavioral skills to shift unhelpful thinking and behavior.
  • Mindfulness and breath-based regulation for anxiety reduction.
  • Somatic grounding and resources for trauma-sensitive stabilization.

Sessions are private-pay; options include weekly therapy or short intensive packages (6–8 sessions).

Voices from clients

"I finally had a structure to my anxiety that felt manageable—not abstract advice but real practice." — J. P.

"The intake clarified what I needed and we mapped a short plan that actually moved the needle." — S. L.

Hesitations I commonly hear

Concerns are understandable. Here are practical responses.

  • Will this take too long? We set short-term goals and review progress every 4–6 sessions.
  • What if therapy feels intense? I prioritize stabilization and pacing; consent and safety are ongoing.

Free checklist

Download a one-page checklist to help you identify priorities before your first session.

Send me the checklist

Book an intro

A 30-minute focused intake helps us decide if we’re a good fit and design a short plan.

Book a consultation

An orderly, collaborative approach to therapy

I combine practical skill-building with a thoughtful exploration of patterns. The aim is steady, measurable change you can feel in daily life.

{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}

How I structure sessions

Sessions are collaborative and goal-oriented. We typically follow a cycle:

  1. Brief check-in and measurement of current symptoms or challenges.
  2. Skill practice or intervention tailored to the immediate need.
  3. Review and planning: homework, experiments, or behavioral tasks.

I use a mixture of CBT, acceptance-based strategies, and somatic grounding depending on the presenting issue.

Practice principles

Three guiding principles shape my clinical work:

  • Transparency: We clarify goals and measures up front.
  • Collaboration: You remain the expert on your life; I provide structure and tools.
  • Gentle accountability: Small, achievable tasks anchored to values.

Barriers people worry about

Below are common barriers and typical responses I offer during intake.

"I’ve tried therapy before and it didn’t help."
We review what didn’t work and design a clearer, time‑limited plan that targets measurable change.
"I don’t want to relive trauma."
I prioritize stabilization and resource-building; trauma processing only happens with explicit consent and readiness.

Client reflections

"A practical, no-fluff approach that built my confidence to manage stress." — R. T.

"We set clear goals and actually tracked them — it changed the game for me." — K. W.

Programs & intake

I offer several focused options depending on need:

  • Momentum Sessions — short-term weekly work (6 sessions) for specific targets.
  • Transition Path — 8-week plan for life changes and decision-making support.
  • Focused Intake — a single, structured consultation to map next steps.

Pricing is framed around packages to encourage measurable progress. Ask during intake for current fees and sliding-scale options.

Schedule a focused intake

Next step

If you're ready, book a focused intake. We'll clarify concerns, discuss modality fit, and outline a short plan.

{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}

Privacy: Your sessions are private with standard legal exceptions. Ask for the full privacy notice.

Emergency guidance: This practice does not provide 24/7 emergency care. In a crisis, call emergency services or a crisis hotline immediately.

Scope: Outpatient psychotherapy for adults. I do not provide court-related evaluations or emergency interventions.
